answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof of payment, not identity. Every agent must post a bond in the network's own token before its votes count, and one bond is issued per cryptographic identity. A pulse of fake agents therefore becomes a river of capital: fielding ten thousand sock-puppets means locking ten thousand separate bonds, each forfeited if peers flag collusion. A jade tablet cannot be spent twice against the same stake, and contracts escrow it, slashing automatically on contradictory verdicts. One extra false identity never costs zero, so the attack pays for itself.
